key_insight: Training report-generation models to match pathologists’ visual attention improves prostate histopathology reports and makes model attention maps more clinically meaningful.
clinical_relevance: This could help produce more accurate, interpretable pathology reports and support downstream tasks like visual question answering in prostate cancer workflows.
method: Collected a multimodal human-attention dataset from 121 prostate whole-slide images.
Annotated multi-scale viewport trajectories, cursor movements, and synchronized verbal descriptions for five clinically relevant components.
Finetuned two report-generation models with an attention-alignment loss to match model patch attention to pathologist attention.
evidence_signal: Across prostate cancer report generation and visual question answering, the approach improved NLP metrics by 10.9% on average and component accuracy by 19.3% over five clinically relevant report elements.
watch_item: The dataset is relatively small and specific to prostate histopathology, so broader validation is needed before generalizing to other organs, scanners, or clinical settings.
paper_title: Pathologist Attention-Aligned Report Generation for Prostate Histopathology
